retrospective.harder_than_needed: The story brief characterized MarmotContext.tsx's five serialiseProfileUpdate call sites as 'a mix of interactive user-initiated sends and background/relay sends' without saying which was which, and publishProfileUpdate — the one method whose own doc comment calls it the 'explicit' publish path — turned out to have ZERO production callers anywhere under app/src or app/pages at story start (confirmed by grep before concluding it was genuinely dead code). Assuming it really was unwired, the first implementation pass added a dev-only window.__fewTest.publishProfileUpdate hook so an e2e test could drive it directly. A second, wider grep (this time including app/pages/, which the first pass had missed) turned up the real caller: app/pages/profile.tsx's handleNicknameBlur -> broadcastProfile -> publishProfileUpdate(next), fired on blurring the nickname field. The dev hook was then removed in favor of driving the real UI, per CLAUDE.md's 'publish through the app' rule — but this cost a full extra investigation + implementation + removal cycle that a scope note pointing at profile.tsx up front would have avoided.
retrospective.surprised_by: onHistorySynced's profilePublishedRef Set (a 'this group's profile was already auto-published this session' guard) was marked BEFORE the signing attempt even started, not after — a pre-existing latent bug that happens to be exactly the failure shape VQ-S8-006 warns about (a locally-cached 'sent' flag set optimistically ahead of the actual send outcome). It was in-scope to fix under AC-SEND-10's 'no residual local state implying success' requirement, but the story task did not call it out as a known issue.
